correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the classifier independently: for 0<β<π/2, a meridian fibre at φ is a line segment in the unit (H,V) disk exactly when (M−Rs cosφ)^2≤q²+s² cos²φ, where s=sinβ and q=cosβ. The sublevel set in u=cosφ is an interval since the coefficient of u² is (R²−1)s²>0. Its containment of both, one, or neither of ±1 gives the full angle circle, one arc, or two arcs, respectively, for a plane that hits; the segment bundle is trivial on the circle (the continuous direction (−q,s cosφ) never vanishes), and over each arc the fibre collapses only at the ends. This proves the annulus/disk/two-disks classification off null boundaries. The toroidal Jacobian gives density (1+H/R)/π and Φ uniform. For fixed β>0 and Rs>1 the two disk caps have half-width arccos(1−δ±/[(R+H)s]), with clipping when necessary, where δ±=1+sH±qV∈[0,2]. Their scaled limits follow from arccos(1−y)∼√(2y); a constant times s^(-1/2) bounds the scaled probability for Rs≥4 and also for Rs<4 by the trivial probability bound. This is integrable under s dβ; the semicircle projection and β-integral give the stated gamma quotient. In the annulus layer put t=Rs<1, then the Jacobian after scaling by R² is t/√(1−t²/R²); it is dominated for R≥2 and offset threshold equality has zero probability. Integrating in t gives E[τ²]/2, and splitting on V+cosΦ≥0 by symmetry gives the stated tangent-half-angle integral and 16/(9π²). The complementary topology and Crofton baseline follow, with disk offset numerator tending to 2 and annulus numerator asymptotic to 1/(6R²) against normalizer 1+πR/4. The supplied checker was read, not run: its grid discretizes the same topology inequalities, not an independent classification of the geometry.
residual_risks: Finite quadrature is corroboration only; limiting proof is for circular ring tori with the stated joint sampling law.

value.rationale: A natural sampling change in random sections changes both rare topology exponents, not just normalization. The exact constants quantify two different mechanisms: an azimuthal cap near projection extrema for disks and a shrinking tilt cone for annuli. These are usable benchmarks for random planar sections taken through interior points rather than for an arbitrary subcase of Crofton sampling.
residual_risks: No extension to other meridians or practical finite-R error bounds is established.
